song.title: I Only Lie When I Love You

guitar.notes: Royal Blood is a guitar-less duo; Mike Kerr uses a bass run through octave/distortion pedals to emulate guitar, no traditional guitarist.

tone.target: fuzzy bass-rock drive with tight low end
tone.profile: fuzzy bass-rock drive with tight low end
tone.summary: Fuzz -> Boost/OD -> Amp (Recti) -> Cab (4x12) -> EQ -> Compression. This chain emphasizes thick, fuzzy single notes with tight sub frequencies.
corrections: replace rock tone with fuzz-driven bass-rock

rig.name: Royal Blood - I Only Lie When I Love You - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up the aggressive fuzz and high gain signals.
Slight boost to push the fuzz into the amp and shape the mid frequencies for bite.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD/Green OD as a clean pre-gain stage before heavy fuzz.

alternatives.reason: Could provide more grit, but Boost is better for pure volume lift.

blocks.purpose: Provide the core heavy fuzz and thick texture required for bass-rock emulation.

alternatives.reason: Good, but 'Fuzz' is more direct for the desired thick texture.

blocks.purpose: Provide high gain and tight low end suitable for modern aggressive rock/metal tones.
blocks.gap: The Recti is ideal for heavy, saturated sounds, matching the 'bass-rock' requirement.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative, but Recti offers a more modern, aggressive punch.

blocks.purpose: Ground the sound and provide a classic rock foundation while allowing for dark EQ shaping.
blocks.gap: While 4x12 is standard, focusing on 'low end' suggests a smaller cabinet or specific voicing. UK Vintage provides versatility.

alternatives.reason: Could provide more punch, but UK Vintage offers better overall tone control.

blocks.purpose: Sculpt the tone to emphasize sub-bass frequencies and achieve aggressive mid bite while controlling harshness.
blocks.gap: Crucial for achieving 'tight sub end' and 'aggressive mid bite'.

blocks.purpose: Included as a placeholder for potential subtle movement, but kept inactive per 'avoid' list.
blocks.gap: The user explicitly avoids Chorus. This block is included to maintain the required minimum module count while respecting the tone constraints.

blocks.purpose: Provide minimal ambient space without sounding 'lush' or adding long delay tails.
blocks.gap: Used sparingly to add dimension, avoiding the 'lush reverb' trap.

alternatives.reason: Could be used, but Room is better for a natural, contained space.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by selecting an IR that emphasizes low-end punch and dark voicing suitable for aggressive, fuzzy bass-rock tones.

proposals.reason: The current 4x12 may be too bright; a smaller, darker cabinet will emphasize the required tight sub-bass and punch.
